name: BigQuery
sku: BigQuery Standard edition. Governance features that need Enterprise or Enterprise Plus carry an enterprise-tier constraint. BigQuery ML and Dataform are not scored here; Dataform has its own record.
tier_name: BigQuery Enterprise or Enterprise Plus edition

store.warehouse.note: A fully managed data platform with a storage layer and a separate compute layer that scale independently, and a serverless architecture with no infrastructure to manage.

serve.query-engine.note: ANSI-standard SQL queries, plus Python through BigQuery DataFrames, on the serverless compute layer.

transform.code-transform.note: BigQuery DataFrames lets Python users analyse and transform data in BigQuery. SQL transformation workflows are scored under Dataform.

store.table-format.note: Supports open table formats Apache Iceberg, Delta and Hudi through BigLake tables and managed Iceberg tables.

ingest.batch-extract.note: Loads batch files in Avro, Parquet, CSV and JSON. It loads what is handed to it; it does not pull from source systems, which Datastream and others do.

ingest.stream-ingest.note: The Storage Write API streams rows in continuously.

bands.note: Dynamic data masking obscures a column for chosen users while still letting them query it, with rules such as nullify, SHA-256 hash, default value, email mask and random hash, attached through policy tags. The editions page lists it under Enterprise and Enterprise Plus only; Standard has no access to fine-grained security controls.

IAM predefined roles and permissions at the project, dataset, table, view and routine level, available on every edition. Column-level policy tags add finer control but need Enterprise or Enterprise Plus, so they are scored under masking instead.

presentation.tagline: Serverless data warehouse with SQL, Python, open table formats and column masking.

cost.note: On-demand queries are $6.25/TB scanned with the first 1TB/month free, and storage is $0.023/GiB/month with the first 10GiB free; a small prototype often stays inside both free allowances.
Third-party estimate: a small analytics team scanning about 10TiB of queries a month with 1TB of active storage runs roughly $75/month on-demand.

Third-party estimate for 10TB storage and 50TB of monthly queries is about $445/month; widened upward for heavier query volume. Committed-use slot pricing can cost less than on-demand at sustained high volume and is not scored here.
